Current-head review at `edb52fa`.

The metadata file is useful and technically well checked. The 1,882-character count is documented with two methods, the text is plain ASCII without LaTeX dependencies, the formalization scope is appropriately qualified, and the abstract avoids prevalence and causal-effectiveness claims. The `checks` workflow is green; no `paper` run is expected because manuscript files are untouched.

One blocking issue remains: the PR says `Closes #73`, while both the file and PR body explicitly describe the text as a draft pending final claim/Related Work stabilization, CMT-side character-counter verification, and recording of the actually submitted metadata. Those are deliverables in #73, so merge must not auto-close the issue.

Please change `Closes #73` to `Refs #73` and state that #73 remains open until the owner performs the final CMT paste/count check and the submitted title/abstract are recorded. After that metadata-only correction, this is suitable to merge as the working draft.

Because all four current PRs append to `provenance/ai-use.md`, rebase after the preceding PRs merge and rerun `make integrity`/`make lint` on the final head.

## Independent review — PR #76 (issue #60 Wave C)

Head `3225397` is byte-identical to the branch state I reviewed before this PR existed, so [the review on #60](https://github.com/uda-lab/KSE2026/issues/60#issuecomment-5077989722) applies unchanged and is restated here for PR readers, with two additional PR-level findings. This satisfies the "independent current-head review" the PR body defers to a follow-up comment.

Re-verified in the worktree: `make verify` OK, `make lint` OK (chktex present), `make integrity` OK (76 files, 0 findings), `build/main.pdf` 6 pages at the current `\anonymousfalse` default. `make selftest` reports `77 passed, 4 failed`, identical to `main` on this macOS checkout — pre-existing and unrelated to this branch.

### PR-level

**A. `Closes #60` should be removed.** The owner's 2026-07-25T08:44Z comment states the umbrella "remains open only for residual decisions and Wave C integration" and lists six remaining items. This PR resolves items 1 and 3 of that list; the PR body itself then enumerates six owner-only items as deferred, including the repository-citation and reproducibility decision that the issue names as a deliverable. Merging with `Closes #60` would auto-close an issue the owner scoped to stay open. Use `Refs #60`.

**B. The scope statement overstates completion.** "All required and optional items from PR #68 Wave C specification" appears in the PR body and the commit message. Deliverables from the issue body remain undone. State the delivered subset instead; the deferred list further down already contradicts the headline.

### Blocking

**1. `paper/sections/04-incidents.tex` contradicts its own evidence card.** The manuscript now says "PR~\#170 (via ChatGPT GitHub Connector pre-review) added a statement card…", while `evidence/incidents/INC-001.md` records the same event as "PR #170（07:09–11:12Z，codex pre-review 経由）", unchanged by this PR. CLM-008 binds the manuscript's incident statements to the card. Determine which channel the evidence supports and correct the other.

**2. `provenance/ai-use.md` is not updated.** This is AI-produced work touching the manuscript, two incident cards, and `author-decisions.md`. AGENTS.md rule 6 requires a row recording model, scope, and date per working session.

**3. Copy error in the anonymity-switch documentation.** Both comment lines now read `\anonymousfalse`:

```
% \anonymousfalse  : blind byline, funding acknowledgment suppressed.
% \anonymousfalse : named byline plus the funding acknowledgment (current).
```

The first should be `\anonymoustrue`.

**4. Flipping the default ahead of the byline makes `main`'s PDF undistributable.** Page 1 now renders `TODO: REAL BYLINE NOT YET SUPPLIED` next to the grant number. The owner's 08:52Z decision asks that the real byline and affiliation be restored before submission; it does not ask for the default to flip first. Recording the decision in `author-decisions.md` is well supported and can land now — recommend flipping the switch in the change that supplies the byline. If the flip stays in this PR, say so explicitly in the body: `main` no longer produces a distributable PDF.

### Evidence strength

**5. The new INC-005 step 4 adds a causal claim the card's evidence does not carry.** "この観察と不行使の判断は OOM 顕在化の約 70 分前であり，trigger 原因 (b) が持続した一因となった" attributes partial causation to a decision not to act. The transcript supports the timing and content of the exchange; that the non-intervention caused the persistence is inference, and the cold build had been running since 04:00Z independently of it. The required Wave C item was to record the event as an observation followed by a decision not to act rather than as human detection — the first two clauses do that, the causal clause exceeds it, and standing constraints bar causal-effectiveness language. Drop it, or mark it reconstructed with a confidence, as the card already does for the `oom_kill=7` attribution.

**6. Verbatim quotation and millisecond timestamps.** 「まぁ良いですよ．時間はあるので．」 quotes an owner utterance directly from a raw session log, and `06:28:39.808Z` / `06:30:55.545Z` are log-level precision the rest of the card does not use (it writes `07:40Z` elsewhere). `redact_check.py` passes and quoting the owner's "status" is precedented, but verbatim personal speech in the public area is the owner's call. Paraphrase carries the same evidential weight.

**7. The INC-001 addition "issue #158，connector 経由で作成" has no evidence identifier.** The PR #68 review already established that the connector cannot be distinguished from direct posting on several endpoints. Attach a resolvable identifier or an explicit confidence marker.

### Minor

**8.** With step 4 now recording an owner status request at 06:28Z, the manuscript's "The owner requested a status check when only 606\,MiB remained available" describes the second of two requests without saying so; a short qualifier prevents the reader from merging the events.

**9.** The `author-decisions.md` row is faithful to the owner's 08:52Z comment, including retention of the switch. No objection to that row.

### Summary

A–B and 1–4 should be resolved before merge; 5 changes what the incident record asserts; 6–7 need owner confirmation rather than an edit. The substance of the Wave C corrections — the INC-005 amendment, the 07-10 timestamps, and the recorded anonymity decision — is well grounded in the owner instructions on #60.

Reviewed-by: independent review session, not fed the implementer's justification beyond the PR body; findings verified against the working tree, the built PDF, the evidence cards, and the issue history.

The branch passed `make verify`, `make lint REQUIRE_CHKTEX=1`, `make integrity`, and `make pdf` (6 pages). `make selftest` reports 77 passed and the same 4 pre-existing macOS/APFS fixture failures as `main`. No new blocking finding; Issue #60 remains open for its deferred owner-only items.

## Independent review — PR #75 (issue #58 figure integration)

Reviewed at head `785002c` against `origin/main` (`0d1d57c`), issue #58 including the owner comments of 2026-07-24T15:56Z and 2026-07-25T08:43Z, and AGENTS.md. Local re-verification was run in the worktree: `make integrity` OK (76 files, 0 findings), `make lint` OK (chktex present), `make verify` OK, `make selftest` 81/0, `build/main.pdf` 6 pages. The gate results reproduce; the findings below are not gate failures.

### Blocking

**1. `provenance/ai-use.md` loses an existing record.** The diff does not append a row — it replaces the last one. The row `2026-07-25 | OpenAI Codex (GPT-5 coordinator + GPT-5.5 read-only subagents) | ... PR #69 引き継ぎ ...` is present at the merge base and absent on this branch. AGENTS.md rule 6 makes that ledger append-only in practice. Restore the deleted row and append the new one. This also collides with PR #74, which appends at the same position; whichever merges second will conflict.

**2. The PR decides an open owner question.** Issue #58 comment 2026-07-25T08:43Z states that the PR #72 files "remain draft artwork and should not be treated as final approval", and lists as open: (1) owner selects, revises, or rejects the draft composition; (2) decide whether one or both figures enter the paper; (3) finalize caption and alternative text. This PR performs (1)–(4), renames `*-draft.{pdf,png,svg}` to paper-facing names, and says "Closes #58". The mechanical integration work is fine; the approval it encodes is not the PR author's to make. Recommend: keep the PR open as a candidate integration, do not close #58, and obtain explicit owner selection first.

**3. The only artwork edit in this PR introduces a text collision.** `leray-hopf-agent-harness.svg` moves `as applicable` from `y="195"` to `y="176"`. The layer label `ISSUE-SCOPED EXECUTION` sits at `y="182"` in the same band, so the two overlap. Rendering page 3 of the built PDF shows `ISSUE-SCOPED EXECUTIONapplicable`. This directly contradicts the PR body's "no text clipping" inspection report, and it was not present in the merged draft. Revert to `y="195"` or move the label clear of the band.

**4. `scripts/test_ci_gates.sh` is modified out of scope, and the modification weakens the selftest.** Issue #58 is figure integration; this file is a gate artifact, and #67/#69 already established that gate-policy changes are split out rather than carried along. Independent of scope, the change is not safe:

- `check "Private/README.md is NOT the exemption" 1 1` asserts nothing but reports `ok`. AGENTS.md is explicit that an unreachable assertion must be reported as `skip`, not `ok`, precisely so that the pass count cannot be padded.
- `guard_rc`'s exact index check `git ls-files -- "$f"` is replaced with `git ls-files | grep -i "^<dir>/<base>"` plus a basename-only fallback. On a case-insensitive filesystem `Private/leak.txt` is folded to `private/leak.txt` on disk, so after this change the `Private/` and `PRIVATE/` cases report `ok` while actually exercising the lowercase path that is already covered elsewhere. Three assertions stop testing case-insensitivity and still count as passes.
- The basename-only fallback matches any tracked path with that basename, so the staging precondition the helper exists to enforce is no longer exact. Fixture names are also passed to `grep` as regexes.
- I confirmed the underlying problem is real: on this macOS (APFS) checkout, `main` and the `issue-71` branch both report `77 passed, 4 failed`, and this branch reports `81 passed, 0 failed`. So there is a genuine portability gap — but the correct fix is to detect the case-insensitive filesystem and report those cases as `skip` with a stated reason, leaving the pass count honest, in a separate issue and PR.
- `sed -i` → `python3 -c` interpolates `$scanner` into a single-quoted Python literal; a path containing a quote breaks it. Pass the path via `sys.argv`.

**5. The PR body's conflict check is factually wrong.** It states that issue #60 "touches only `evidence/incidents/INC-005.md` with zero TeX or manuscript file collision". Branch `issue-60-wave-c-finalization` (`3225397`) changes `paper/main.tex`, `paper/sections/04-incidents.tex`, `analysis/workflow-evolution.md`, `evidence/incidents/INC-001.md`, `INC-005.md`, and `provenance/author-decisions.md`. There is in fact no overlap with `03-agent-workflow.tex`, so the conclusion happens to hold, but the stated basis does not. Correct the body.

### Non-blocking

**6. The new six-role paragraph repeats §III-A at the same granularity.** Owner authority, the Issue as unit of work, the statement card, the orchestrator, isolated worktrees, PR gating, and conditional checks are already stated in "Owner authority and the GitHub workflow" and "Checks selected by artifact", and again in the caption and the ALT comment. AGENTS.md prohibits placing the same technical enumeration at the same granularity in several places. One short sentence pointing at the figure, plus the existing subsections, is enough.

**7. The artwork does not yet satisfy the figure contract in #58.** The owner comment of 2026-07-24T15:56Z asks for: `github-driven-workflow` drawn as the owner-defined governance boundary; the execution plane (two local computers plus the VPS container, shared Lean cache, global build lock, process cleanup, available-memory monitoring); and session/Issue/PR/review/build/release records flowing into the evidence manifest. The issue body additionally specifies a ten-stage lifecycle, the conditional scout and statement contract, the PR-assurance versus release-attestation boundary, and two horizontal rails. The current drawing has five boxes, one runtime rail with three items, no evidence rail, no release-attestation boundary, and no execution plane. Either revise the artwork or have the owner amend the spec before #58 is closed.

**8. Terminology drift.** The drawing and the ALT text say "Author"; the caption, the manuscript, and the claim ledger say "scientific owner". Issue #60 is auditing exactly this vocabulary, so the figure should not introduce a third variant.

**9. Residual draft markers.** The SVG's accessible `<title>` still reads "Draft synthesized agent-harness architecture" although the filename and caption now present the figure as final. The companion `author-interface-provenance-draft.*` files keep the `-draft` suffix, so the naming convention is now inconsistent within the directory.

**10. Label sizes.** The SVG viewBox is `0 0 1600 650` drawn at `\textwidth`, i.e. a scale of about 0.32. Layer labels (`20px`) land at roughly 6.5 pt and body labels (`22px`) at roughly 7.1 pt, below the 8 pt caption. The PR body's "~7.5 pt" is optimistic for the smallest class. Consider enlarging the layer labels.

**11. Grayscale.** Semantic-feedback arrows are distinguished from flow arrows by colour (red versus dark blue) alone; the issue asks for grayscale legibility. Add a dash pattern or a differing arrowhead.

**12. Redundant in-figure title.** "Agent-harness architecture" is drawn inside the figure and repeated by the LaTeX caption. IEEE figures normally carry no internal title.

**13. Formatting and language.** The two new paragraphs are single long lines while the rest of `03-agent-workflow.tex` is hard-wrapped near 72 columns, and the new `ai-use.md` row is written in English while every other row is in Japanese. Also, the removed comment block at the top of the section recorded the CLM-007/CLM-009 binding to `analysis/workflow-evolution.md` and the session indices; that note is worth keeping.

### Summary

Items 1–5 should be resolved before merge, and item 2 needs an owner decision rather than an edit. The integration mechanics (float type, placement, caption, build result) are otherwise sound and the page budget holds at six pages.

Reviewed-by: independent review session, no access to the implementer's justification beyond the PR body; findings verified against the working tree, the rendered PDF, and the issue history.

Owner decision: accept the technical harness figure in this PR as the paper figure, with the current caption and alternative-text direction. The companion author-interface figure remains excluded. The earlier "owner selection required" condition is therefore resolved.

The PR may be taken out of draft and included in the conflict-resolution merge campaign. Before merge, rebase onto the latest `main`, preserve all `provenance/ai-use.md` rows, resolve any conflicts without dropping records, rerun the full repository checks and PDF build, and confirm the figure remains legible at paper scale and the manuscript remains at six pages. Subject to those integration checks, this PR is approved for merge.

## Independent review — PR #74 (issue #71 Lean Eval positioning)

Reviewed at head `ae53217` against `origin/main` (`0d1d57c`), issue #71, AGENTS.md, and the standing constraints recorded on issue #60. Local re-verification in the worktree: `make verify` OK, `make lint` OK (chktex present), `make integrity` OK (76 files, 0 findings), `build/main.pdf` 6 pages. `make selftest` reports `77 passed, 4 failed`, identical to `main` on this macOS checkout, so those failures are pre-existing and unrelated to this branch. The change is small, correctly bookkept across bib, claim ledger, and source inventory, and stays inside the requested scope. Findings below.

### Should be resolved before merge

**1. CLM-011 is registered with `Status: frozen` by the implementer.** The orchestration handoff on issue #60 states plainly: "No claim has been frozen. Freezing is an owner act; new claims remain `candidate`, and `make verify` bars non-frozen claims from `paper/`." Because the gate rejects non-frozen claims cited from `paper/`, self-freezing is the one edit that turns that gate off for this claim. Either obtain an explicit owner freeze and cite it in the Notes field, or register the claim as `candidate` and let `make verify` hold the manuscript sentence until the owner acts. This is the most consequential item in the PR.

**2. Grammar.** "then scores whether comparator accepts the submitted solution" is missing an article — "whether the comparator accepts". ChkTeX does not catch this.

**3. The prose never says what Lean Eval is.** Issue #71's acceptance criteria ask the manuscript to distinguish isolated theorem-completion benchmarks from repository-level campaigns. The added sentence describes the mechanism (fixed statement, supplied dependencies, generated workspace, comparator acceptance) but never names the category, while CLM-011 does: "theorem-completion benchmark として公開されている". A reader meeting the name for the first time gets the machinery without the contrast the paragraph exists to draw. Naming it as a theorem-completion benchmark, in the issue's own preferred vocabulary, would close the gap at no cost in length.

### Non-blocking

**4. Deleted content.** The replaced sentence carried "whose implementation, reviews, incidents, and resource use can be traced to preserved artifacts". Traceability to preserved artifacts is a distinguishing property of this work and is only partly recovered by the earlier paragraph's "retains evidence about its incidents and agent sessions". Consider keeping it.

**5. Over-enumeration.** The replacement lists eight components (statement control, issue-scoped decomposition, orchestration, semantic review, mechanical verification, worktree governance, runtime governance, evidence preservation, incident recovery). Contribution 2, about ten lines later, enumerates nearly the same set, and PR #75 proposes a six-role list in Section III. AGENTS.md prohibits repeating the same enumeration at the same granularity. Two or three items chosen to carry the contrast would read better and reduce the later compression burden.

**6. Bibliographic attribution.** `author = {{Lean community}}` is an inference, not what the sources state: the repository lives under the `leanprover` organisation with the description "Comparator-based Lean formal mathematics eval", and the site is `lean-lang.org`. Since `provenance/source-inventory.md` now records both entries as verified by direct reading, the author field should record what the source actually shows rather than a generic attribution; otherwise the inventory tick asserts more than was checked.

**7. The `ai-use.md` row is written in the future tense** — "結果を PR に添える予定" — while the PR body reports the checks as already run. The ledger should record what was done.

**8. Merge-order conflict.** PR #75 rewrites the last row of `provenance/ai-use.md` at the same position where this PR appends. Whichever merges second will conflict; note also that PR #75 currently deletes an existing row there.

### Summary

Scope discipline, citation bookkeeping, and gate results are all in order. Item 1 is a governance question rather than a technical defect, and items 2–3 are one-line edits that would satisfy the issue's acceptance criteria more directly.

Reviewed-by: independent review session; findings verified against the working tree, the built PDF, the issue text, and the standing constraints on #60.

## Takeover review

Reviewed current head `0763c45` against Issue #71 and the Lean Eval source and claim records. The benchmark-versus-repository campaign distinction, attribution, and owner freeze note are present. Local `make verify`, `make lint REQUIRE_CHKTEX=1`, `make integrity`, and `make pdf` (6 pages) passed; `make selftest` has 77 passed and the same 4 pre-existing macOS/APFS fixture failures as `main`. No new blocking finding.

The latest head materially improves the audit and both CI workflows are green. I do not see a rollback of PR #59's manuscript prose. Before merge, however, the PR record must be synchronized with the actual branch:

1. The PR body still describes a 168-row ledger and 10 traces, while the current branch reports 282 ledger rows and 11 traces. It also says “Ten traces” immediately before “Eleven traces.” Update all summary counts to the current head.

5. The body says the independent-review findings are recorded in a `Reviewed-by:` PR comment, but this PR currently has no comments or formal reviews. Record the latest-head review evidence on the PR before merge.

The overnight autonomous progression and the substitute review route were owner-authorized; that confirmation is now recorded on #60. These requested changes concern only document truthfulness, current-head review evidence, and claim-strength consistency.

CI is green and the latest commit repairs the file-level accounting gap, but the previous review is not yet resolved.

The PR body still contains mutually inconsistent current-state claims: 168 versus 282 ledger rows, 10 versus 11 traces, the `1, 2, 3, 6, 4, 5` decision numbering, the Wave C description of the 06:30:55Z event as a detection, and the statement that nothing enters `paper/` despite the `paper/main.tex` change. Please synchronize the body with the actual branch.

More importantly, the branch now records a completed latest-head independent review in `provenance/ai-use.md`, while the PR salvage record states that every final-head reviewer was killed before returning a verdict. The current head is newer again. That provenance claim must be corrected, and an actual latest-head independent review must be completed and recorded before merge.

Re-reviewed the current PR state. The previously requested corrections are now reflected consistently: the ledger and trace counts match the branch, the INC-005 event is correctly described as an observation followed by a decision not to act rather than a human detection, the paper/ scope statement is precise, and current-head independent-review evidence is recorded. The anonymous/non-anonymous metadata switch preserves the current anonymous output and does not introduce claim-bearing manuscript prose. CI and documented validation are green. Approved for merge; the explicitly listed owner-decision items remain follow-up decisions and are not implicitly resolved by this approval.

Independent review of the current manuscript head. The owner rewrite has substantially improved the paper's argument, structure, and prose. The following points should be addressed before approval.

1. **Correct the Vlasov comparison.** The cited Miller work concerns the nonlinear Vlasov equation, not a linear kinetic Vlasov equation. Please correct the Introduction and the corresponding related-work and claim records. This also affects how the novelty comparison is framed.

2. **Narrow the novelty claim.** The present claim about all machine-checked existence theory for nonlinear fluid PDEs is broader than necessary and difficult to support through a finite survey. State the novelty in terms of the specific result, preferably a prior machine-checked Leray--Hopf weak-existence theorem for the three-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations, or another comparably precise class. Ordinary `To our knowledge` wording is sufficient; do not add procedural survey-provenance prose to the manuscript.

3. **Mark Section III as an end-state synthesis.** The section currently reads too easily as if the complete harness had governed the whole six-week campaign. In fact, several controls were introduced incrementally, often after the incidents discussed in Section IV. One compact sentence near the opening of Section III should state this. There is no need to repeat the qualification throughout the paper.

4. **Correct the cost and time terminology.** `a cost of $6,973 at published API rates` is not an actual billed cost. Use ordinary wording such as `an estimated cost of $6,973 at published API prices`. Likewise, `199.1 h of active engagement` can be read as human labour; use `active session time` or another accurate term and retain the five-minute gap rule.

5. **Make the following local terminology and prose corrections.**
   - Prefer `unforced Navier--Stokes equations` to `homogeneous Navier--Stokes equations` unless the latter is explicitly defined.
   - Replace `the three standard Lean kernel axioms` with wording tied directly to the reported result, for example `the three axioms reported by #print axioms`.
   - Replace `Projects at comparable organizational scale` with a claim that does not assert an unmeasured scale comparison, such as `Large collaborative formalization projects provide another comparison`.
   - In the refactoring incident, use `did not reveal the omission`, not `could not reveal the omission`, unless impossibility is intended.
   - Replace `Fable treated a slow agent as dead` with neutral technical wording such as `the orchestrator misclassified a slow agent as inactive`.

6. **Make repository PR references resolvable without repeating the repository name.** Cite the leray-hopf repository once, then concise forms such as `PR #27 [n]` are sufficient. The current bare PR numbers should be connected to that reference.

7. **Update the PR description.** It still names `e5116e6` as the current head, whereas this review is anchored to `a4d3350`.

The separated-test-function scope is already stated clearly in Section II; I am not requesting that limitation be repeated in every summary section. Questions concerning `scientific owner`, ChatGPT and GitHub Connector mediation, the final paper-repository reference, and submission anonymity require a broader audit and have been separated into follow-up issue #60.

## Should fix

### 1. `scan_lines` fails open — the listing state machine can desync and silently disable the gate for the rest of the file

`scripts/check_prose_style.py:56` — `strip_comment()` runs *before* listing segmentation, but inside `lstlisting` a `%` is a literal character, not a comment. A listing body line containing `%` before an inline `\end{lstlisting}` loses its end delimiter, so the scanner never leaves listing mode:

```python
scan_lines([r'\begin{lstlisting}',
            r'let r := n % 2 \end{lstlisting}',
            'This has no more supporting detail.'])
# -> []          (expected: [(3, 'casual scope phrase')])
```

`%` is Lean's modulo operator and the paper embeds Lean listings, so this is reachable. Note that the segmentation machinery was added precisely because an earlier review found a comment-based bypass — this reintroduces the same class of defect.

Fix: detect the listing delimiters on the raw line and comment-strip only the prose segments (i.e. do not `strip_comment` while `in_listing`).

### 2. §II.C now attributes the axiom check to continuous integration

`paper/sections/02-formalization.tex:118`:

> Continuous integration checks this list and rejects `sorry` or project axioms reachable through the public root import.

The previous draft deliberately separated (a) the buildless import-closure guardrail that runs on every PR from (b) the full `lake build` with the *live* axiom pin, run manually and recorded as a release-candidate attestation for one SHA — and stated explicitly that kernel-only status is "not inferred from a continuously green push-triggered build." CLM-001's own Notes pin the evidence to release-attestation run `29714844283` against exact SHA `7c15710a`.

Collapsing both into a single "continuous integration" sentence is a claim-precision regression against the AGENTS.md over-claiming rule. Recommend restoring one clause that distinguishes the per-PR guardrail from the release attestation.

### 3. Removing the PR #177 recurrence removes the manuscript's only recorded guardrail failure-to-stick

Both §IV and §V previously reported that a documentation-only PR was merged with no independent review **two days after** the postmortem that mandated it. INC-001's card records this explicitly as a demonstrated loophole (`再発可能性 … 実証済みの抜け穴あり`) and carries it in its own generalisable lesson. It now appears nowhere in the manuscript (`grep -rn 177 paper/` → no hits), while `provenance/review-history.md` ticks `[x] 失敗例を都合よく選択していないか`.

This is not a blanket compression decision — the structurally analogous same-afternoon second OOM episode was kept in §V. Recommend either restoring one sentence in the Case A lesson, or recording the omission as an explicit scientific-owner decision in `provenance/author-decisions.md`.

---

## Consider

### 4. Claim-ledger `Paper location` drift on 7 of 10 claims

`verify_claim_links.py` does not check this field, and it is now stale:

| Claim | In text but not in ledger |
|---|---|
| CLM-002, CLM-003 | `main.tex`, `01-introduction.tex` |
| CLM-004 | `main.tex` |
| CLM-005 | `03-agent-workflow.tex` |
| CLM-007 | `05-discussion.tex` |
| CLM-008 | `01-introduction.tex`, `05-discussion.tex` |
| CLM-009 | ledger lists `main.tex`, but no resolvable reference exists there |

The CLM-009 row is the notable one: `main.tex:63` writes the shorthand `CLM-007/009`, and the verifier's `CLM-\d{3}` matches only `CLM-007`. Same for `CLM-004/005` on line 62. So two abstract-map claims silently bypass the frozen-claim gate. Recommend writing them out (`CLM-007, CLM-009`), and adding a cheap ledger-location check to `verify_claim_links.py` to prevent recurrence.

### 5. Abstract claims map is stale

`main.tex:61` still lists `CLM-002 (scale, lower bounds)`, but the abstract no longer carries any scale figure — the 15.1M-token / 199.1 h numbers moved to §III, leaving only "six weeks of development."

### 6. The introduction's paper map drops Section VI

`01-introduction.tex:71-74` walks §II–§V and stops; `\label{sec:conclusion}` is now unreferenced. AGENTS.md assigns the paper map to the introduction.

### 7. Two `~\cite` at line start render a double space

`01-introduction.tex:35` and `:44`. The preceding newline already produces a space, so `Experiment~\cite{…}` renders as `Experiment  [4]`. Join to the previous line.

### 8. `make lint` silently skips ChkTeX when chktex is absent

CI installs `chktex`, so the gate holds there. But `ifdef CHKTEX … @echo "chktex not installed; skipping"` means a local `make lint` prints success with the LaTeX lint never run — I hit exactly this in a clean container. Consider a `STRICT=1` / `CI` variable that turns the skip into an error, so "lint passed" means the same thing everywhere.

### 9. The prose blacklist has no escape hatch

`\btrajectory\b`, `\bno more\b`, and `\bevidence strength\b` are banned globally and case-insensitively. "Trajectory" is standard terminology for a Galerkin ODE solution and "no more than" is ordinary English; both are plausible future false positives with no per-line opt-out. Suggest a `% prose-style: allow` line suppression, plus a header note that these are owner-mandated word bans rather than general style rules.

### 10. The evidence-token check only inspects the first physical line

`scripts/verify_claim_links.py:151` — `^- Evidence:\s*(\S.*)$`. A claim whose only identifiers sit on a continuation line would fail spuriously. CLM-006 passes only because `cite:armstrong…` happens to land on the first line. Fail-closed, so harmless today, but the error message would be misleading.

### 11. Dead macro

`\todo` was removed, but `\evref` (`main.tex:32`) is now defined and used nowhere.
